- When sentiment turns sharply bullish (e.g., +1.00) followed by a spike in news volume, model tends to overreact and overshoot true price — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- If sentiment shows strong negative momentum (e.g., -1.00) and news volume drops, model underreacts — adjust downward by 3–5% to avoid mean-reversion lag.
- After a strong upward spike in sentiment (e.g., +1.00) with high news volume, true price often lags — forecast should be slightly conservative (down 2–5%) to account for delayed momentum.
- When sentiment is neutral or mixed (e.g., 0.00–0.67) and news volume is low, model tends to overestimate mean reversion — reduce forecast by 2–4% to avoid premature correction.
- If sentiment shows consistent downward trend (e.g., -0.33 repeated) and price is trending down, model often underestimates the slope — increase forecast by 1–3% to capture momentum.
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently underestimates late-period spikes — add 1–3% buffer to forecast if sentiment turns bullish in last 5–7 days.
